thread:
Devin: Heads-up — noticed p99 on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate jumped ~200ms after yesterday's routing-policy tweak. Not sure if it's a true latency regression or percentile math artifact. :eyes:
Tess: Did you check sample counts? If the routing change moved a chunk of traffic to a sampled path we might be downsampling different buckets, which breaks t-digest merges.
Devin: I pulled the slice for that endpoint — sample_count dropped from ~18k to ~2k for the affected cohort. p50/p95 stayed similar. p99 moved a lot.
Aj: Sounds like classic low-sample p99 noise. But we also recently changed to route some traffic through the fallback pool that strips caller tags. That could change aggregation keys and merge different distributions.
Samir: Also remember quota fallback will route heavy requests to the cheaper pool and we apply aggressive ingress sampling there to protect telemetry costs. So the p99 you see might be computed on a different sampling regime.
Tess: Agreed. Two practical asks: 1) expose sample_count next to each percentile in the UI (tiny badge), 2) surface sample_origin (ingress/sampled/tdigest-merge) in the tooltip so users know what drove the number.
Devin: I like that. Would reduce triage time. For the tooltip maybe this text: "p99 computed from downsampled t-digests (source: ingress-sampled, n=2,130)".
Aj: Implementation note: our rollup currently merges t-digests without carrying raw sample counts per route. We need to propagate a count metric alongside the digest. Should be safe — add `sample_count` in the rollup proto and UI can read it.
Tess: Can we also flag low-confidence percentiles? e.g., if n < 1000 show a small warning icon and hover text: "low sample confidence — p99 unstable".
Samir: Yes — low-sample badges + the sample origin will help. But watch out: quotas and routing changes can cause quick swings. We should store the merge-mode and routing-weight snapshot in the event that created the rollup so post-hoc debugging is easier.
Aj: Quick prototype idea: in the aggregator, expose two numbers: `merged_count` and `raw_count`. merged_count = sum(weights used for tdigest merge, raw_count = total samples seen before downsampling. UI shows both if available. Backend falls back to merged_count when raw_count missing.
Devin: Nice. Also let's add a backend check rule: if p99 delta > 50ms and sample_count dropped > 75% in same window, annotate the dashboard with "likely sampling or routing artifact" so oncall doesn't chase a phantom regression.
console-bot: deploy-bot: alert created: "pctl-samplecount-badge RFC" — PR template issue opened at https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/4231 by Tess.
Tess: I'll flesh out the RFC and the UI mock (small badge + tooltip + low-confidence icon). Assigning to Aj for aggregator changes and Samir for routing/telemetry sampling audit.
Aj: I'll prototype the rollup proto change and add tests for preserving counts during t-digest merges. ETA EOW.
Samir: I'll run a quick scan to find other endpoints where quota fallback correlates with sample_count drops and paste results in the issue.
Devin: Perfect. Thanks — this should make p50/p95/p99 much more actionable. :thumbsup:
Tess: Filing follow-ups in the issue: UI mocks, proto spec, backend migration plan, rollout gating for the change.
Devin: Cool, keep updates in the issue thread and ping me if you need product acceptance criteria.
